basics.name: vmName
basics.label: Virtual machine name
basics.toolTip: Name of the virtual machine that will run LibreDB Studio.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-40 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; must start with a letter and must not end with a hyphen.

basics.name: adminUsername
basics.label: Linux admin username
basics.toolTip: Administrator account used for SSH access to the virtual machine.

toolTip.authenticationType: SSH public key is strongly recommended.
toolTip.password: Password for the Linux administrator account.

elements.name: vmSize
elements.label: Virtual machine size
elements.toolTip: LibreDB Studio runs comfortably on 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM.

elements.name: osDiskSizeGb
elements.label: OS disk size (GB)
elements.toolTip: LibreDB Studio keeps its SQLite storage on the OS disk.

elements.name: dnsLabelPrefix
elements.label: DNS name label
elements.toolTip: Produces <label>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com. Must be unique inside the region.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-63 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; must start with a letter and end with a letter or number.

elements.name: appAdminEmail
elements.label: Application administrator email
elements.toolTip: The email address you will sign in to LibreDB Studio with.

elements.name: appAdminPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for the LibreDB Studio administrator account (not the VM account).

constraints.validationMessage: 12-64 characters. Letters, digits and ! @ # % ^ * _ + = . , : ? - are allowed.

elements.name: enableHttps
elements.label: Enable HTTPS with a free Let's Encrypt certificate
elements.toolTip: Issues a certificate for the DNS name above. Requires inbound port 80 to be reachable from the internet.

elements.name: acmeContactEmail
elements.label: Certificate contact email (optional)
elements.toolTip: Sent to Let's Encrypt for expiry notices.

constraints.validationMessage: Leave empty or enter a valid email address.

elements.name: appSourceAddressPrefix
elements.label: Allowed source for the web interface
elements.toolTip: Use 'Internet' for public access, or a CIDR such as 203.0.113.0/24 to restrict it.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter 'Internet' or a valid IPv4 address / CIDR range (octets 0-255, prefix /0-/32).

options.text: This restriction applies to port 443, where the application is served. Port 80 stays open to the internet so that Let's Encrypt can issue and renew the certificate; it serves the challenge and a redirect to HTTPS. If no certificate can be issued, the application stays on port 443 with a self-signed certificate instead of moving anywhere else, so your restriction is never widened and the deployment URL stays valid; your browser will warn you until a trusted certificate arrives.

elements.name: sshSourceAddressPrefix
elements.label: Allowed source for SSH (optional)
elements.toolTip: Leave empty to block inbound SSH completely. Azure Bastion or the serial console can still be used.

constraints.validationMessage: Leave empty or enter a valid IPv4 address / CIDR range (octets 0-255, prefix /0-/32).

options.text: Inbound SSH will be blocked. You can still manage the VM with Azure Bastion or the serial console, and you can add an SSH rule to the network security group later.
